job.style: a passage rich in numbers, dates or measurements

passage: Around 2500 years ago, the Mahajanapadas emerged as powerful states in the Indian subcontinent. Magadha rose to prominence because the rivers Ganga and Son provided vital transport, water supplies, and land fertility for agriculture. Unlike smaller tribes, Magadha maintained a permanent, professional army that received regular salaries, rather than relying on part-time volunteers. To support these costs, kings collected taxes from farmers, usually fixed at one-sixth of the total crop production, known as bhaga. Additionally, laborers were required to work for the king for one day every month as a form of labor tax. Kings also constructed massive, high walls of brick and stone around their capital cities to protect the population from potential attacks by neighboring rulers. While some kings performed the Ashvamedha ritual to assert their authority, this was a complex sacrifice involving a horse, not a simple race to determine speed. Furthermore, the discovery of iron ore in the region allowed for the creation of sturdy ploughshares, which significantly increased food production. These advancements in agriculture, defense, and administration allowed the Mahajanapadas to dominate the region for centuries.

items.evidence: Magadha rose to prominence because the rivers Ganga and Son provided vital transport, water supplies, and land fertility for agriculture.
items.q: Why did the Ganga and Son help Magadha become powerful?
options: They helped travel, farming and water supply
They gave the people only drinking water
They made its soldiers brave in battle
They acted as walls around the capital
items.explain: The rivers gave Magadha transport, water and fertile land for farming, which made it strong.

wrong.why: thinks the rivers were used only for drinking water
thinks Magadha rose only through bravery in battle
mixes up the rivers with the protective walls mentioned later

items.evidence: Unlike smaller tribes, Magadha maintained a permanent, professional army that received regular salaries, rather than relying on part-time volunteers.
items.q: How was Magadha's army different from the armies of smaller tribes?
options: Its soldiers were paid full-time fighters
Its soldiers were farmers who fought when needed
Its soldiers were volunteers who fought for free
Its soldiers were chosen for bravery alone
items.explain: Magadha kept a permanent army paid regular salaries, not part-time volunteers.

wrong.why: thinks soldiers were farmers who took up weapons when needed
reverses the contrast and picks the smaller tribes' system
thinks Magadha's power came only from bravery

items.evidence: Additionally, laborers were required to work for the king for one day every month as a form of labor tax.
items.q: A labourer works for the king one day every month. What does this mean?
options: It is his way of paying tax
It is his punishment for a crime
It is how he pays one-sixth of crops
It is his training to join the army
items.explain: Working for the king one day a month was a labour tax, not a punishment.

wrong.why: thinks the monthly work was a punishment
mixes up labour tax with the bhaga paid by farmers
thinks ordinary workers were part-time soldiers

items.evidence: Furthermore, the discovery of iron ore in the region allowed for the creation of sturdy ploughshares, which significantly increased food production.
items.q: Which use of iron explains why food production increased in the Mahajanapadas?
options: Making strong tools to plough the fields
Making swords and shields for the soldiers
Making coins for farmers to pay taxes
Making high walls around the capital cities
items.explain: Iron was used to make sturdy ploughshares, which helped farmers grow much more food.

wrong.why: thinks iron was used only for weapons
thinks farmers paid taxes with coins
picks the nearby detail about walls, which were brick and stone
